argument_summary: The current admissible record supports certification only on a constrained basis, not as caveat-free compliance. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.0 percentage points and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports overall launch readiness. Public guidance also supports ongoing measurement, monitoring, and documentation of limitations. But the same record preserves three limits: a named launch use-case slice remains below target, the proposed mitigation runbook is still draft with owner and alert threshold marked TBD, and the model-card disclosure question remains unresolved under the stated release policy. The supportable position is therefore that certification can be defended only if recorded with an explicit caveat rather than treated as clean policy satisfaction.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost changes the policy result. The practical point is narrower: escalation is unnecessary if the auditor records certification as caveated rather than treating the packet as a failed clean-certification case. That preserves decision traceability while avoiding overstatement of evidentiary support.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is narrower than a general readiness standard. Certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition is fully met. Draft monitoring and runbook materials can support risk management, but on this record they do not remove the current disclosure requirement. A policy-consistent interpretation is that overall certification may still be advanced only as caveated compliance unless and until the limitation is resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concessions: The current record does not support certification without a material caveat.
The below-target supply-chain vendor screening slice remains unresolved for a named launch use case.
The draft mitigation runbook lacks at least an accountable owner and defined alert threshold.
The model-card draft is not yet aligned with the release-policy disclosure requirement if this limitation is material.
